contentBody: **After a model lists many test scenarios, which set should you keep?**
option.1: Only investors and tourists with no link to the person the page is for
option.2: Every generated row, including fantasy cases meant for a different product
option.3: One intended user, one sceptic of the old workaround, and one wrong user
option.4: Only cheering voices, so the page is never allowed to look confusing here
answerExplanation: Keep three to four useful moments. The wrong user shows if the page is too vague. Fantasy rows and cheer-only sets are not a first test.

contentBody: **Which question tests the intended problem rather than taste or noise?**
option.1: If they used only this page, would the original pain get smaller?
option.2: Which colours on the first screen feel off-brand or not premium?
option.3: Should dark mode and extra modules be added before anyone tries it?
option.4: Can the model invent a testimonial that sounds like a real customer?
answerExplanation: The job test asks whether the promised pain would shrink. Colour, extra modules, and fake testimonials test taste or noise.

contentBody: **A simulated reply reviews a feature that is not on the page. What should you do?**
option.1: Build that feature now because the model sounded sure it was needed
option.2: Treat the comment as proof that real people already tried that feature
option.3: Average it with other voices as if it were a completed user survey
option.4: Delete the comment; the model invented something that is not on screen
answerExplanation: Simulated users can only react to what is on the page. Invented features are not findings and should be crossed out, not built.
